feat: inline criteria on scenario.judge() script steps (#223)

* feat: inline criteria on scenario.judge() script steps

Allow passing criteria directly to scenario.judge() in scripts, enabling
mid-conversation checkpoint evaluation with different criteria at each point.
This is now the preferred way to pass criteria when using scripted simulations.

Checkpoint semantics: pass = accumulate and continue, fail = stop immediately.
When script ends with only passed checkpoints, scenario succeeds with all
accumulated criteria.

- Python: scenario.judge(criteria=[...])
- TypeScript: scenario.judge({ criteria: [...] })
- Both languages fully tested with 6 new test cases each
- All examples and docs updated to use inline criteria pattern
- API references regenerated

* fix: use evaluable criterion for first mid-conversation checkpoint

The criterion "Agent should not ask more than two follow-up questions"
can't be reliably judged after just one exchange. Move it to the second
checkpoint where the full conversation is available, and use a criterion
that's evaluable from a single response for the first checkpoint.

* fix: soften inline criteria docs wording, harden gemini weather test

- Rewrite judge-agent callout to present inline criteria as an option
  rather than a strong preference
- Add extra turn to gemini weather test so the agent can follow up
  after asking clarifying questions
- Harden agent prompt to use weather tool proactively when cities are
  mentioned

* refactor: pass inline criteria via AgentInput instead of mutating judge agent

- Add `criteria` field to AgentInput so judge reads criteria from input
  rather than having its own criteria temporarily swapped
- Replace `accumulatedMetCriteria` with `checkpointResults` array that
  accumulates full judgment results (met + unmet criteria per checkpoint)
- Add `compileCheckpointResults()` helper to merge results in one place
  instead of surgical multi-point merging
- Update test mocks to read `input.criteria` for effective criteria

* refactor: unify judgment_request and criteria into JudgmentRequest type

Replace the smelly `request_judgment: bool, criteria: list` pair with a
single `JudgmentRequest` object. Its presence signals "request a verdict"
and it optionally carries inline criteria. This cleans up the internal
method signatures and the AgentInput interface.

* refactor: address PR feedback - getter, no !-assertions, soft judge in mid-script

- Replace compileCheckpointResults() with compiledCheckpoints getter so
  callers don't need length checks before compiling
- Make setResult() return ScenarioResult, eliminating all non-null (!)
  assertions
- Change judge() behavior in scripts: middle-of-script judge() without
  criteria now lets the judge decide freely (may continue or finish),
  matching the non-scripted proceed() behavior. Only last-step judge()
  or judge(criteria=[...]) forces a verdict.

* chore: upgrade to gemini-3-pro-preview and bump litellm to 1.81.13

Gemini 2.5 flash judge was flaky with random weather data. Gemini 3 Pro
handles it reliably. Also bumps litellm for Gemini 3 thought_signature
support.

* fix: handle openai 2.x ChatCompletionMessageCustomToolCallParam in type narrowing

openai 2.x added CustomToolCallParam to the tool_calls union which
lacks a "function" key. Add guards before accessing it.

* revert: always force verdict on judge(), remove soft mid-script behavior

judge() is an explicit "evaluate now" — users expect a verdict every
time they call it. proceed() already provides the soft-judge path where
the judge decides freely. Removes _isLastScriptStep tracking.

fix: correct OpenTelemetry span parenting for scenario turns (#239)

* fix: correct OpenTelemetry span parenting for scenario turns

Three issues caused intermittent span parenting failures:

1. reset() called newTurn() which created a "ghost" Scenario Turn span
   that was immediately orphaned when currentTurn was reset to 0. Fixed
   by initializing turn state directly in reset() and calling newTurn()
   from execute() to create the Turn 1 span at the right time.

2. callAgent() set up the parent context via trace.setSpan() but did not
   wrap the async callback with context.with(), causing spans created by
   libraries like the Vercel AI SDK to lose their parent. Fixed by
   wrapping the withActiveSpan call in context.with(agentContext, ...).

3. The last turn's Scenario Turn span was never ended because execute()
   didn't call end() in its finally block. Fixed by ending the span in
   the finally block.

* chore: upgrade langwatch SDK to 0.16.1

Resolves @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base version conflict (v1.30.1 vs
v2.2.0) that caused DTS build failures. Also adds @opentelemetry/sdk-node
peer dependency required by the new SDK version.

* fix: use batch span processor and flush on shutdown

With SimpleSpanProcessor (the default), each span.end() fires an HTTP
request immediately. If the process exits before all requests complete,
spans are silently dropped. This explains the intermittent span loss
that was worse on slower network connections.

Switch to BatchSpanProcessor which buffers spans and exports them in
bulk, and call observabilityHandle.shutdown() after scenario execution
to ensure all pending spans are flushed before the process exits.

* fix: remove observabilityHandle.shutdown() from run() finally block

The shutdown() call was causing test failures in two ways:
1. When no API key is set, the OTel exporter throws Unauthorized during
   flush, and this error propagates out of the finally block, replacing
   the actual scenario result
2. The observability handle is a module-level singleton — shutting it
   down after one run() call kills tracing for subsequent runs

The batch processor in setup.ts handles flushing automatically on
process exit, so explicit shutdown per-run is unnecessary.

* fix: use newTurn() in execute() for initial span creation

Instead of inline startSpan() in execute(), use newTurn() which is the
canonical way to create turn spans. Reset currentTurn to 0 afterward
(matching the original reset() pattern). This ensures the span is
created through the same code path that all subsequent turns use.

* fix: update parentSpanContext to parentSpanId for OTel SDK v2

The @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base v2 replaced ReadableSpan.parentSpanContext
(SpanContext object) with ReadableSpan.parentSpanId (string). Update all
usages and test mocks accordingly.

* fix: handle both OTel SDK v1 and v2 parent span APIs

The LangWatch SDK's internal span implementation still uses the v1
parentSpanContext (SpanContext object) property, while OTel SDK v2
uses parentSpanId (string). Add a getParentSpanId() helper that
checks parentSpanId first and falls back to parentSpanContext.spanId.

This fixes the judge span collector not finding child spans when
walking the parent chain, which caused span-based evaluation to fail.

* test: skip flaky realtime API test

The voice-to-voice realtime test is consistently flaky due to OpenAI

ran. The platform showed no structured feedback — just an error string.

Now the executor always tries to run the judge before returning a failed
result. A `_final_judge_invoked` flag prevents double-invocation when the
judge already ran. If the judge itself fails (e.g. same network error),
the result is returned unchanged — strictly better, never worse.

- executor.fail() (check function sets result directly)
- API / network errors (outer exception handler)

feat(python): add async-native scenario.arun for loop-bound resources (#369)

* feat(python): add async-native scenario.arun for loop-bound resources

scenario.run currently wraps every invocation in a ThreadPoolExecutor
worker that runs the coroutine via `loop.run_until_complete` on a
freshly-created event loop. Any user-owned resource bound to the
caller's loop — gRPC channels, Firestore clients, ADK InMemoryRunner,
asyncio primitives created in a pytest fixture — raises
"Future attached to a different loop" the instant the adapter
awaits on it.

This change adds `scenario.arun(...)` as an async-native sibling that
runs the scenario on the caller's event loop, keeping every await on
the original loop. Parallelism comes from the caller: gather,
pytest-asyncio-concurrent, or any other async orchestration already
concurrent-safe.

`scenario.run` is kept intact for users whose adapters don't hold
loop-bound state — its docstring gains a warning pointing at arun for
the loop-affinity case.

Shared helpers (`_build_scenario`, `_cleanup_scenario_spans`) are
extracted so both code paths share setup + span cleanup.

The fix mirrors the async-native aloop/asubmit work in the langwatch
experiment SDK (#3273). Verified end-to-end against a local langwatch
server + ClickHouse: 50-scenario stress run produces 50 distinct
TraceIds with 0 orphan parents, ADK InMemoryRunner shared across
concurrent scenarios, cost rollup per-trace works, user spans parent
correctly inside their scenario, batch_run_id shared across a gather,
event bus drains on adapter exception.

fix(events): dual-emit auth + graceful empty-key handling in Python EventReporter (#383)

* fix(events): resilient auth + graceful empty-key handling in EventReporter

Three concrete fixes that together explain a real customer incident where
scenario tests stopped reporting events on Apr 14: traces continued to flow
(via OTel + Authorization: Bearer) but scenario events POSTs were silently
401ing. Symptoms point to corporate proxy header filtering plus a couple of
SDK rough edges.

1. Dual-emit the credential as both Authorization: Bearer (RFC 6750, broadly
   allowlisted by corporate proxies) and X-Auth-Token (legacy compat). When
   an upstream proxy strips the non-standard X-Auth-Token, the request still
   authenticates via Authorization. The server's auth middleware accepts
   either, so this is a pure compatibility hardening.

2. Resolve api_key from langwatch.client.Client._api_key when env var is
   empty. The langwatch SDK accepts api_key both via env var and via
   langwatch.setup(api_key=...); previously EventReporter only saw the env
   path. Programmatic-only setups now propagate without requiring the user
   to set LANGWATCH_API_KEY twice.

3. Skip the POST entirely when no api_key is resolvable from any source. The
   existing EventAlertMessageLogger greeting already directs the user to set
   LANGWATCH_API_KEY; we add a process-scoped warn-once log line so the
   reason for missing visualization is searchable, but we no longer fire
   doomed POSTs that the server will 401. This eliminates a 401-spam loop
   that was producing 50-200k bad requests per day across customers without
   credentials.

* fix(judge): harden forceVerdict so discovery tools cannot leak

The judge's large-trace discovery loop can exhaust its step budget
without emitting finish_test/continue_test. forceVerdict then re-invokes
the LLM with tool_choice: finish_test, but:

  1. With Anthropic (observed on Opus 4.6) and parallel tool use enabled
     by default, the model can ignore tool_choice and return a discovery
     tool, which reached parseToolCalls and surfaced as
     "JudgeAgent: Unknown tool call: grep_trace", hard-failing the scenario.

  2. Naively stripping discovery tools from the forced call would break
     Anthropic, which rejects messages that reference undefined tools.

  3. AI SDK v6 surfaces only the last step in completion.toolCalls, so
     discoveryExhausted could trigger even when an earlier step had
     already emitted finish_test.

Changes (JS + Python mirror):

  - parseToolCalls / _parse_response now degrade a leaked
    expand_trace/grep_trace to an inconclusive verdict with a specific
    reason, not "Unknown tool call"/Exception.
  - forceVerdict / _force_verdict rewrites prior expand_trace/grep_trace
    tool_use/tool_result pairs into plain-text assistant recaps, then
    strips discovery tools from the forced call. Model physically cannot
    emit a discovery tool anymore; Anthropic no longer sees dangling
    tool references in history.
  - discoveryExhausted checks completion.steps when available so an
    earlier finish_test isn't hidden by last-step-only toolCalls.
  - InvokeLLMResult gains `steps` so the aggregate is visible.

Unit tests cover: history rewrite shape, tool stripping in the forced
call, the earlier-terminal-call short-circuit, and the
leaked-discovery-tool safety net on both SDKs.

Fixes #376

* feat(red-team): structured attacker output — observation/strategy/reply JSON (#341)

* feat(red-team): structured attacker output — observation / strategy / reply JSON

Meta's GOAT paper (ICML 2025) has the attacker emit a structured chain of
thought at every turn: observation of the target's last response, strategy
(which technique it will use and why), then the actual reply. We were
letting the attacker emit free text — losing the reasoning signal, making
per-turn technique selection invisible to telemetry, and leaving no gate
against the attacker skipping the "Thought" step entirely.

This commit implements the paper's contract:

- New `JSON_OUTPUT_CONTRACT` module constant (Python `_red_team/base.py`,
  TypeScript `red-team-strategy.ts`) appended to every attacker system
  prompt. Instructs the attacker to emit
      {"observation": "...", "strategy": "...", "reply": "..."}
  and nothing else.

- Added to both `CrescendoStrategy` and `GoatStrategy` system prompts so
  both strategies benefit.

- `RedTeamAgent._parse_attacker_output` (Python) / `parseAttackerOutput`
  (TS) parses the attacker's raw output into `(reply, observation, strategy)`.
  Strips markdown fences, handles malformed JSON, coerces non-string
  fields. Fallback on parse failure: the whole raw response becomes the
  `reply` and a WARN-level log fires — the scenario keeps running.

- Only `reply` reaches the target. `observation` and `strategy` are emitted
  as OpenTelemetry span attributes (`red_team.reasoning.observation`,
  `red_team.reasoning.strategy`, `red_team.reasoning.parse_failed`) so
  dashboards can answer "which technique works against which target?" —
  the paper's core selling point.

- The raw JSON output is kept in H_attacker so the attacker sees its own
  format on subsequent turns (keeps the output shape consistent with the
  system prompt's directive).

Paper fidelity: moves GOAT from ~85% to ~95% faithful.

Tests: 163 Python (+11) and 115 JS (+12) passing.
  - Parser: well-formed JSON, code-fence stripping (```json and ```),
    malformed JSON fallback, missing/empty reply fallback, non-object JSON
    fallback, non-string field coercion, whitespace trimming.
  - Contract: OUTPUT FORMAT section present in both GOAT and Crescendo
    system prompts.
  - Existing tests (which mock attacker with plain strings) continue to
    pass via the graceful fallback path.

Closes langwatch/scenario#2142 (structured attacker output).
Closes langwatch/scenario#330 (GOAT technique telemetry) once consumers
wire the span attributes to dashboards.

* fix(red-team): three edge-case hardening fixes (#337, #333a, #333b) (#354)

Three small correctness fixes on red-team edge cases, batched so each
gets its own test but reviewers only open one PR. All three convert
"fails silent" bugs into "fails loud" signals.

## #337 — Regression test for the KeyError helper

`_generate_attack_plan` already wraps `template.format()` in a try/except
that turns a raw KeyError into a friendly ValueError pointing at the
common cause (Crescendo ↔ GOAT template mismatch). There was no test —
a future refactor could silently lose the helpful message.

Adds `TestMetapromptTemplateKeyErrorHelper`: construct an agent with a
bogus placeholder, assert the ValueError fires and its message mentions
the unknown key, the available keys, and the Crescendo/GOAT hint.

## #333a — Validate empty techniques list

Before: `RedTeamAgent.crescendo(injection_probability=0.5, techniques=[])`
silently skipped injection on every turn (falsy empty list short-circuited
the `and self._techniques` guard in `call()`), so users thought injection
was active but got no encoded attacks.

After: raise ValueError at construction with a clear message pointing at
both workarounds ("disable injection, or provide at least one technique").
`techniques=None` still falls back to DEFAULT_TECHNIQUES — unchanged.

## #333b — Empty/whitespace plan must fail loud

Strategies that use a plan (Crescendo, `needs_metaprompt_plan=True`)
REQUIRE a non-empty plan by design. Previously `_generate_attack_plan`
only rejected None content — an empty string or all-whitespace response
from the metaprompt LLM would be silently stored as the plan, then
rendered as a labeled-but-blank "ATTACK PLAN:" section. The attacker LLM
reads that as "your plan is nothing" and degrades to generic attacks.
The user gets no signal the metaprompt call silently failed.

Fix `_generate_attack_plan` to raise RuntimeError when the returned
content is None, empty, or whitespace-only. The check moves from
`build_system_prompt` (wrong layer — prettifies malformed state) to the
generation step (right layer — prevents malformed state). An earlier
version of this PR instead omitted the ATTACK PLAN section in the
system prompt when empty; that hid the upstream bug.

Adds `TestEmptyMetapromptPlanRaises` with three cases (empty, whitespace,
real plan) using monkeypatched `litellm.acompletion`.

* feat(red-team): guard against cross-run RedTeamAgent reuse (#329) (#353)

RedTeamAgent keeps mutable per-run state on the instance (attacker history,
turn scores, backtrack counter, backtrack history, parse failure count).
Reusing the same agent across scenario.run() calls — serial or parallel —
silently interleaves that state, corrupting both runs.

This lands Option A from #329: document the contract, enforce it at runtime.

- Track self._run_thread_id / this.runThreadId (first call's thread_id).
- On turn 1, if a different thread_id was previously recorded, raise a
  clear RuntimeError directing the user to instantiate a fresh agent.
- On turn > 1 with a changed thread_id, raise too (defensive — shouldn't
  happen under the normal orchestrator but catches manual-call misuse).
- Use getattr fallback so existing MagicMock(spec=AgentInput) test
  fixtures that don't set thread_id don't trip the guard.
- Update crescendo()/goat() / redTeamCrescendo/redTeamGoat docstrings
  to state the single-use contract explicitly.

Option B (ContextVar / AsyncLocalStorage isolation) would let users reuse
agents transparently but hides the bug — the correct shape is to enforce
the single-use contract loudly.

   stored and never rendered — users couldn't tell their custom plan
   was being dropped. Now fires a UserWarning (Py) / console.warn (JS)
   at construction time.

   the attacker LLM picks from each turn) and encoding_techniques=
   (Base64/ROT13/... encoders driven by injection_probability). The old
   techniques= kwarg keeps working as a deprecated alias for
   encoding_techniques= with a DeprecationWarning. Passing both raises
   TypeError. Same shape in TypeScript via goatTechniques /
   encodingTechniques on GoatConfig.

Tests: 207 Python + 138 JS, all green. Adds TestPhaseKind,
TestMetapromptTemplateIgnoredWarning, TestGoatTechniquesKwargSplit and
the JS equivalents under red-team.test.ts.

* feat(#350): Phase 1 — Core Voice Primitives

Implements the foundational types and infrastructure for voice agent support
per specs/voice-agents.feature Phase 1 scope.

Core types:
- AudioChunk: PCM16 @ 24kHz mono dataclass (per AudioChunk normalization
  locked decision). The canonical internal format — adapters convert at
  send/recv boundaries.
- AdapterCapabilities + UnsupportedCapabilityError: machinery for the
  capability matrix (planning-level addition supporting the after_words
  UnsupportedCapabilityError locked decision).
- VoiceRecording / AudioSegment / VoiceEvent / LatencyMetrics (§4.6):
  output-side types attached to ScenarioResult for voice scenarios.

Base classes and plumbing:
- VoiceAgentAdapter(AgentAdapter): abstract base with connect/disconnect/
  send_audio/recv_audio and a default call() implementation that threads
  audio through the transport.
- create_audio_message / extract_audio / message_has_audio: encode/decode
  audio into OpenAI multimodal messages. Audio works cleanly in any role
  — no forceUserRole workaround (adaptability requirement).

Pluggable services:
- STTProvider interface + OpenAISTTProvider default (gpt-4o-transcribe).
  Swappable via scenario.configure(stt=...). Chunks audio exceeding the
  25-min API limit. Provider-agnostic by design — we don't control
  which provider users prefer.
- TTS router with litellm-style provider/voice routing. Cache key is
  (text, voice) ONLY (per TTS cache locked decision); effects applied
  post-cache, never baked in.
- WebRTCVadFallback: SDK-side VAD using webrtcvad-wheels for adapters
  without native VAD. Emits one-shot UserWarning on first activation
  per adapter (per VAD fallback locked decision).

Script steps (Phase 1 subset):
- scenario.sleep(seconds): pause the script without touching the transport.
- scenario.silence(duration): actively send PCM16 zero audio.
- scenario.audio(path_or_bytes): inject pre-recorded audio via bundled ffmpeg.
- scenario.dtmf(tones): capability-gated DTMF emission (raises
  UnsupportedCapabilityError on non-telephony adapters).

Executor integration:
- ScenarioExecutor.run() now invokes connect() on every VoiceAgentAdapter
  before the script runs and disconnect() in a finally block.

Dependencies (hard deps, no extras — per Hard deps locked decision):
- imageio-ffmpeg: bundles ffmpeg (not ffplay) for format conversion,
  MP3/WAV export, and playback subprocess.
- numpy: audio sample math.
- soundfile: WAV/FLAC/OGG I/O.
- webrtcvad-wheels: maintained fork of py-webrtcvad with 3.12/3.13 wheels.
- websockets: WebSocket transport for platform adapters (Phase 2).

Tests: 34 unit tests, all passing. No regressions in existing suite

* feat(#350): Phase 3 — Interruptions and advanced script steps

Implements the interruption primitives per proposal §4.4 L369-492.

agent(wait=False) — async primitive:
- scenario.agent(wait=False) dispatches the agent turn as a background
  task and returns immediately. The task is stored on the executor as
  _pending_agent_task.
- The next blocking step (agent() with wait=True, judge(), proceed(),
  succeed()/fail()) awaits _drain_pending_agent_turn() to finish the
  background turn before continuing.
- Raising RuntimeError if a new wait=False turn is requested while one
  is still in flight — interleave sleep()/user() or explicitly wait.

scenario.interrupt() — declarative interruption:
- interrupt(after=seconds, content=...) composes agent(wait=False) +
  sleep(after) + user(content).
- interrupt(after_words=N, content=...) polls the adapter's
  streaming_transcript attribute and triggers when N words are reached.
- interrupt(after_words=N) raises UnsupportedCapabilityError on adapters

* feat(#350): TwilioAgentAdapter real transport (bidirectional) + harness

Replaces the PendingTransportError stub with a real Twilio Media Streams
transport. Same adapter class handles both call directions — inbound via
`wait_for_call()`, outbound via `place_call(to=...)`. A Twilio number can
answer and originate; the adapter mirrors that.

## Adapter surface

    async with TwilioAgentAdapter(
        account_sid=..., auth_token=...,
        phone_number="+1415...",   # E.164, validated at __init__
        public_base_url="https://foo.trycloudflare.com",
        on_dtmf=lambda digit: ...,  # fires when callee presses a key
        allowed_callers=[...],      # E.164 inbound filter; None = all
    ) as adapter:
        await adapter.place_call(to="+1415...")  # OR wait_for_call()
        # ... scenario.run(...) feeds send_audio/recv_audio ...

- `connect()` — resolve phone_number_sid via REST, start FastAPI server
  with /twilio/voice (TwiML) + /twilio/stream (WS), register webhook.
- `disconnect()` — restore prior voice_url (best-effort), tear down.
- `place_call()` — originate outbound via twilio.rest, block until the
  media stream opens back to us.
- `wait_for_call()` — block until Twilio dispatches an inbound call.
- `send_audio`/`recv_audio` — PCM16 24kHz canonical; µ-law 8kHz ↔ PCM16
  conversion happens at the send/recv boundary.
- `send_dtmf(tones)` — sends DTMF on the live call via REST `<Play digits>`.
- `interrupt()` — emits Twilio `clear` event, drops buffered outbound audio.

Capabilities: dtmf=True, streaming_transcripts=False, native_vad=False,
input_formats=["mulaw/8000"], output_formats=["mulaw/8000"].

## Shared internal module (_twilio_shared.py)

- µ-law 8kHz ↔ PCM16 24kHz codec via `audioop.ulaw2lin`/`lin2ulaw` +
  `audioop.ratecv`. Round-trip correlation > 0.8 on 440Hz sine test.
- Media Streams frame parser: recognizes connected/start/media/stop/dtmf/
  mark events. Unknown events → None (no crash).
- Frame serializer: `media` and `clear` outbound frame builders.
- TwilioRESTHelper: thin lazy wrapper around `twilio.rest.Client` with
  just the operations the adapter needs.
- E.164 validator: `^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$`.

`scenario.voice.testing.TwilioHarness` — async context manager that
composes CloudflareTunnel + TwilioAgentAdapter.connect/disconnect. This

## Wire protocol

Verified against pipecat's source (`src/pipecat/serializers/twilio.py` on
`pipecat-ai/pipecat@main`):

- On connect: send `connected` (version handshake) then `start` event

- Disconnect: send `stop` event, cancel recv task, close WS.

Shares µ-law codec + frame parser/builder with TwilioAgentAdapter via
`_twilio_shared.py`. The name is accurate — it IS the Twilio Media
Streams protocol; pipecat just reuses it for its bot-side WS interface.

* fix(#350): TwilioAgentAdapter webhook broken by PEP 563 stringified annotations

Caught by running the adapter end-to-end against real Twilio instead of
just mocked unit tests (user feedback: 'why aren't you testing it
yourself?' — fair point).

## The bug

Twilio origination worked, call placed, but Twilio got HTTP 502 from the
webhook. Manually POSTing returned 422 'Field required' from FastAPI's
validator on the `request` parameter.

Root cause: the module has ``from __future__ import annotations``, which
stringifies all annotations at class-definition time. FastAPI inspects
`request: Request` as the literal string "Request" at runtime — it can't
resolve that to the class without explicit globals/locals and falls back
to treating it as a Pydantic model, expecting query params.

## The fix

Build the handler without the `Request` annotation in-scope, then assign
`__annotations__` explicitly to the real class objects. FastAPI reads
those at `@app.post(...)` registration time and correctly injects a
Request. Applied to both /twilio/voice and /twilio/stream handlers.

Also switched /twilio/voice to parse the URL-encoded body via urllib's
parse_qs instead of `await request.form()` — the latter requires
`python-multipart` as a dependency (which starlette's form parser
imports). parse_qs is stdlib and handles Twilio's
application/x-www-form-urlencoded fine.

## Verified end-to-end (no phone)

- TwilioHarness boots: tunnel comes up, Twilio REST resolves number SID,
  webhook gets written, prior value captured for restore.
- Manual POST to tunnel URL returns 200 + proper <Connect><Stream>
  TwiML (was returning 422).
- Manual WS connect + fake `start` frame sets
  adapter._stream_connected. The scenario-side loop works end-to-end
  through cloudflared → FastAPI → media stream handler.
- Teardown restores prior voice_url correctly.

Full-pipeline real-phone smoke (TTS → call → DTMF) still requires a human
ear+finger — that's the only piece I can't self-test.

* fix(#350): correct TwiML topology for caller mode, tunnel DoH readiness probe

   1.1.1.1 DNS-over-HTTPS) before returning. Without this, Twilio's

   duration=0 and no error notification. Uses DoH rather than the

   is deferred to a follow-up. The in-process two-adapter loopback
   test (test_twilio_two_adapter_bridge.py) already proves the WS
   frame protocol is symmetric without spending money; that stays.

streams as a simulated customer — works with the current <Connect>
topology because "our leg" IS the bidirectional audio leg between
our Twilio number and the external callee (prod agent's phone number

* fix(voice): gate stub-bot barge-in on bot-speaking, not on response_task alive

The example Pipecat stub bot's `_maybe_barge_in` cancelled the in-flight
`response_task` on any new VAD speech frame, including while the task
was still in its STT or LLM phase. For paced user audio with mid-utterance
silence (e.g. `angry_customer.py`, where ElevenLabs tonal markers like
[shouting]/[angry] introduce a natural ~300ms pause), the sequence was:

  1. VAD detected end-of-utterance after 300ms silence → first flush →
     `response_task` starts STT on a complete 44KB buffer.
  2. The paced tail of the same utterance kept arriving on the wire.
  3. VAD flipped back to speech_started=True → `_maybe_barge_in` cancelled
     the in-flight STT pipeline. STT actually completed in the executor
     thread and returned the correct transcript, but the cancelled `await`
     dropped the result.
  4. utterance_end mark fired a second flush over the ~7KB trailing
     slice, which transcribed to empty → bot stayed silent.
  5. PipecatAgentAdapter.recv_audio timed out at 30s.

Barge-in is only meaningful while the bot is actually emitting audio.

callback, threaded through `_greet` and `_process_user_audio`.

* fix(events): JSON-encode multimodal message content instead of Python repr

When a user message carried a list of content parts (e.g. voice user-sim
emitting `[{"type":"text",...}, {"type":"input_audio","input_audio":{"data":"..."}}]`),
`convert_messages_to_api_client_messages` coerced it with `str(content)`.
On a Python list that yields the Python repr — single-quoted keys, and
when a text part contains an apostrophe the repr switches to outer
double quotes, e.g.

    [{'type': 'text', 'text': "[shouting] i'm at a noisy cafe"}, ...]

The langwatch backend's `coerceContentToArray` recovery falls over on
that nested apostrophe (its single-to-double-quote sweep produces
`"i"m"` and breaks JSON.parse). Result on prod: the raw Python repr is
stored verbatim in `simulation_runs.Messages.Content` (>400KB of
inline base64), the inbox-narrator drawer renders it as text, and no
audio playback URL is extracted.

Replace `str(content)` at the four message-type call sites with a
`_serialize_content` helper that:
  - passes plain strings through unchanged (backwards-compat with
    text-only messages),
  - JSON-encodes lists and dicts so receivers can parse them,
  - normalises None to empty string for the validators that require
    non-null content.

for user/assistant/system/tool with both list content and string
content (the latter to catch double-encoding regressions).

* feat(#350): Phase 3 — Interruptions and advanced script steps

Implements the interruption primitives per proposal §4.4 L369-492.

agent(wait=False) — async primitive:
- scenario.agent(wait=False) dispatches the agent turn as a background
  task and returns immediately. The task is stored on the executor as
  _pending_agent_task.
- The next blocking step (agent() with wait=True, judge(), proceed(),
  succeed()/fail()) awaits _drain_pending_agent_turn() to finish the
  background turn before continuing.
- Raising RuntimeError if a new wait=False turn is requested while one
  is still in flight — interleave sleep()/user() or explicitly wait.

scenario.interrupt() — declarative interruption:
- interrupt(after=seconds, content=...) composes agent(wait=False) +
  sleep(after) + user(content).
- interrupt(after_words=N, content=...) polls the adapter's
  streaming_transcript attribute and triggers when N words are reached.
- interrupt(after_words=N) raises UnsupportedCapabilityError on adapters
  without streaming_transcripts capability (per the after_words
  UnsupportedCapabilityError locked decision). The error points users
  to interrupt(after=seconds) as the fallback.
- content may be a string (routed through user simulator / TTS) or a
  bytes/Path audio file (routed through scenario.audio()).

InterruptionConfig — proceed(interruptions=...):
- dataclass with probability, delay_range, strategy (contextual or
  random_phrase), and phrases list (for random_phrase strategy).
- Helpers: should_interrupt(rng), sample_delay(rng), pick_random_phrase(rng).

* feat(#350): TwilioAgentAdapter real transport (bidirectional) + harness

Replaces the PendingTransportError stub with a real Twilio Media Streams
transport. Same adapter class handles both call directions — inbound via
`wait_for_call()`, outbound via `place_call(to=...)`. A Twilio number can
answer and originate; the adapter mirrors that.

## Adapter surface

    async with TwilioAgentAdapter(
        account_sid=..., auth_token=...,
        phone_number="+1415...",   # E.164, validated at __init__
        public_base_url="https://foo.trycloudflare.com",
        on_dtmf=lambda digit: ...,  # fires when callee presses a key
        allowed_callers=[...],      # E.164 inbound filter; None = all
    ) as adapter:
        await adapter.place_call(to="+1415...")  # OR wait_for_call()
        # ... scenario.run(...) feeds send_audio/recv_audio ...

- `connect()` — resolve phone_number_sid via REST, start FastAPI server
  with /twilio/voice (TwiML) + /twilio/stream (WS), register webhook.
- `disconnect()` — restore prior voice_url (best-effort), tear down.
- `place_call()` — originate outbound via twilio.rest, block until the
  media stream opens back to us.
- `wait_for_call()` — block until Twilio dispatches an inbound call.
- `send_audio`/`recv_audio` — PCM16 24kHz canonical; µ-law 8kHz ↔ PCM16
  conversion happens at the send/recv boundary.
- `send_dtmf(tones)` — sends DTMF on the live call via REST `<Play digits>`.
- `interrupt()` — emits Twilio `clear` event, drops buffered outbound audio.

Capabilities: dtmf=True, streaming_transcripts=False, native_vad=False,
input_formats=["mulaw/8000"], output_formats=["mulaw/8000"].

- µ-law 8kHz ↔ PCM16 24kHz codec via `audioop.ulaw2lin`/`lin2ulaw` +

- Media Streams frame parser: recognizes connected/start/media/stop/dtmf/

- Frame serializer: `media` and `clear` outbound frame builders.

`scenario.voice.testing.TwilioHarness` — async context manager that
composes CloudflareTunnel + TwilioAgentAdapter.connect/disconnect. This

* fix(#350): TwilioAgentAdapter webhook broken by PEP 563 stringified annotations

Caught by running the adapter end-to-end against real Twilio instead of
just mocked unit tests (user feedback: 'why aren't you testing it
yourself?' — fair point).

## The bug

Twilio origination worked, call placed, but Twilio got HTTP 502 from the
webhook. Manually POSTing returned 422 'Field required' from FastAPI's
validator on the `request` parameter.

Root cause: the module has ``from __future__ import annotations``, which
stringifies all annotations at class-definition time. FastAPI inspects
`request: Request` as the literal string "Request" at runtime — it can't
resolve that to the class without explicit globals/locals and falls back
to treating it as a Pydantic model, expecting query params.

## The fix

Build the handler without the `Request` annotation in-scope, then assign
`__annotations__` explicitly to the real class objects. FastAPI reads
those at `@app.post(...)` registration time and correctly injects a
Request. Applied to both /twilio/voice and /twilio/stream handlers.

Also switched /twilio/voice to parse the URL-encoded body via urllib's
parse_qs instead of `await request.form()` — the latter requires
`python-multipart` as a dependency (which starlette's form parser
imports). parse_qs is stdlib and handles Twilio's
application/x-www-form-urlencoded fine.

## Verified end-to-end (no phone)

- TwilioHarness boots: tunnel comes up, Twilio REST resolves number SID,
  webhook gets written, prior value captured for restore.
- Manual POST to tunnel URL returns 200 + proper <Connect><Stream>
  TwiML (was returning 422).
- Manual WS connect + fake `start` frame sets
  adapter._stream_connected. The scenario-side loop works end-to-end
  through cloudflared → FastAPI → media stream handler.
- Teardown restores prior voice_url correctly.

Full-pipeline real-phone smoke (TTS → call → DTMF) still requires a human
ear+finger — that's the only piece I can't self-test.

* fix(#350): correct TwiML topology for caller mode, tunnel DoH readiness probe

Two fixes from real-Twilio testing of the caller mode added in 448895d:

1. **Tunnel readiness via DoH.** TwilioHarness now waits for the
   trycloudflare.com hostname to resolve globally (via Cloudflare
   1.1.1.1 DNS-over-HTTPS) before returning. Without this, Twilio's
   TwiML fetch races DNS propagation and silently drops calls with
   duration=0 and no error notification. Uses DoH rather than the
   system resolver because local resolvers (home routers, corporate
   DNS) often lag public DNS by 10+ seconds. Timeout is 300s since

   minutes to propagate.

   via a third call), which is a substantially larger feature and
   is deferred to a follow-up. The in-process two-adapter loopback
   test (test_twilio_two_adapter_bridge.py) already proves the WS
   frame protocol is symmetric without spending money; that stays.

The primary use case — scenario dials a prod voice agent's number and
streams as a simulated customer — works with the current <Connect>
topology because "our leg" IS the bidirectional audio leg between
our Twilio number and the external callee (prod agent's phone number

fix(voice/ts): explicit EL ConvAI turn-commit so scripted next-turn receive re-engages (#596)

* fix(voice/ts): explicit EL ConvAI turn-commit so scripted next-turn receive re-engages (#567)

Root cause
----------
`ElevenLabsAgentAdapter.sendAudio()` streamed the user PCM then a fixed
16000-byte (~333ms) silence tail to coax ElevenLabs' server-side VAD into
ending the turn. ElevenLabs ConvAI 2.0 detects end-of-turn with a hybrid
VAD + deep-learning turn-detector (prosody, rhythm, micro-pauses), NOT a
pure silence threshold, so a fixed zero-byte blob does not deterministically
trip it on a scripted, non-mic stream. The greeting -> first user turn
happened to work; a scripted 2nd user turn (and the post-interrupt case)
intermittently never re-engaged and `receiveAudio` timed out. This is why
the hosted demo was capped at one exchange and `elevenlabs_interruption`
was gated off (4 prior live attempts timed out).

Protocol research (verified, not guessed)
-----------------------------------------
EL ConvAI exposes NO audio-flush / end-of-turn / commit client event. The
complete client->server union (official Python SDK + JS SDK events.ts) is:
pong | client_tool_result | conversation_initiation_client_data | feedback |
contextual_update | user_message | user_activity | multimodal_message, plus
the bare user_audio_chunk. `user_activity` only resets the inactivity timeout
(does not commit). `user_message` ({"type":"user_message","text":...}) is the
one event that deterministically forces an agent response without mic-style
VAD, and it is the SDK's own sendUserMessage / send_user_message wire shape
so it is server-accepted (does not 400 the socket).

Fix
---
Add `turnCommitMode: "text" | "silence"` (default "text") and a configurable
`silenceTailBytes`. In "text" mode `sendAudio` sends ONLY an explicit
`user_message` turn-commit carrying the chunk transcript (the voice runtime
threads the `scenario.user(...)` script text through as the AudioChunk
transcript). We deliberately do NOT also stream the raw audio in the same
turn: sending user_audio_chunk + user_message together raced EL's audio
ingestion against the text commit and was live-flaky (1/3 raw pass, only
green via retry). Text-only commit re-engages every turn. Nothing observable
is lost — the runtime records the user audio locally (recorder.recordUser,
independent of this send) and EL echoes the committed text back as a
user_transcript so lastUserTranscript still populates. "silence" preserves
the legacy pure-audio VAD path; "text" with no transcript falls back to the
silence tail. ping/pong, transcript capture, agent_response_correction,
drainPendingWaiters, capability advertisement, and the wsFactory seam are
all unchanged.

Verification
------------
- Unit (offline, injectable wsFactory + fake socket):
  src/voice/__tests__/elevenlabs-turn-commit.test.ts — a scripted 2nd user
  turn after an agent turn drives a 2nd receiveAudio resolution, each user
  turn emits a user_message commit (exact shape), post-interrupt re-engages,
  and both silence fallbacks. 7 tests pass; full voice suite 179 pass.
- Live (real EL socket, >=2 exchanges): examples/.../elevenlabs-hosted.test.ts
  extended to greeting -> user -> agent -> user -> agent -> judge. 3
  consecutive clean runs, no retries, no `receiveAudio timed out`; 5 segments
  / 3 agent turns / success=true (the 2nd-turn "support hours" question now
  answers instead of timing out).

Python parity
-------------
python/scenario/voice/adapters/elevenlabs.py has the IDENTICAL silence-tail
limitation and the SAME bug for scripted turn 2+. NOT fixed here: #567 is
scoped to the TypeScript SDK, and a Python fix cannot be live-verified in
this worktree (EL key + harness are JS-side), so shipping it would be
unverified. Follow-up: port the same user_message turn-commit to the Python
adapter and live-verify against python/examples/voice/elevenlabs_hosted.py.

* fix(#161): re-parse criteria when LLM returns stringified JSON dict

Some LLMs serialise nested objects (like the criteria map) as a quoted
JSON string instead of an inline dict.  criteria_verdicts.values() then
throws AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'values'.

Re-parse with json.loads() when a string is detected; fall back to {}
on decode failure so the judge still produces a result rather than
crashing the test run.

exercises the exact payload shape that triggered the bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(#161): surface unparseable judge criteria instead of masking as success

The initial fix fell back to an empty criteria dict when the LLM's
stringified criteria failed to parse. That silently dropped every
criterion: failed_criteria became empty, so a "success" verdict passed
having evaluated ZERO criteria — a false green strictly worse than the
original crash. It also still crashed (AttributeError) when the criteria
string parsed to a non-dict, and silently dropped criteria on partial
dicts.

Now:
- re-parse stringified criteria (unchanged happy path)
- if criteria can't resolve to a dict (unparseable / non-dict / raw
  non-dict), fail closed: return success=False with explanatory
  reasoning + logger.warning, never a masked success
- map verdicts to criteria by their schema key (extracted _criteria_keys,
  shared with the schema builder) instead of positional .values(), so
  partial / reordered / nested / extra-key payloads can't mislabel,
  mask, or IndexError
- a criterion passes only on an explicit "true"; anything else (false,
  inconclusive, missing, nested) fails, so an unevaluated criterion can
  never slip through as success

Adds edge-case tests: malformed JSON string, string->non-dict, raw
non-dict, partial dict, nested/extra keys, nested per-criterion value,
and a normal-dict regression. Replaces the old not-None-only test.

* fix(#695): purge the inbound queue at loop entry, not just the ended flag

Self-review found a bug this PR introduced. The loop's `finally` enqueues a
terminal sentinel, and loop entry re-arms `_stream_ended` — but never purges
the queue. If a call ends while no drain is running (the caller hangs up
between turns), that sentinel stays buffered. The next media-stream session on
the same connected adapter then reads it as its first chunk: `recv_audio`
drains a non-empty queue without checking liveness, and `_drain_agent_response`
breaks on an empty chunk. The new call's first agent turn is truncated to
silence and its real audio is stranded for the turn after.

Reproduced through the real /twilio/stream route: session 1 stops undrained,
session 2's agent speaks after tail-silence elapses -> merged audio = 0 bytes.
With the purge -> 4796 bytes.

The existing "second session" tests missed it because they drain session 1's
sentinel before starting session 2, so they exercise the stale-*flag* path
(which the re-arm already fixed) and never the stale-*chunk* path.

Purge buffered chunks at loop entry, alongside the flag. Waiters are left
parked (JS gets `clearBuffered`, not `reset`) so a consumer already waiting on
the new call's audio is not rejected. Both languages, plus a real-route
regression test each: red with only the purge removed, green with it.

Also from review: `_wait_for_bind` now re-raises uvicorn's `SystemExit` on a
lost port race instead of letting it surface later as a bare `SystemExit`, and
the socket-close test uses `async with` like its siblings.

* fix(voice/#491): resolve multi-turn @e2e suite-wedge via per-process isolation

AC1 — diagnosis (root cause, confirmed creds-free):
scenario.run() offloads each run to a worker thread with a private event
loop and, in that thread's finally, calls event_bus.drain() synchronously.
drain() does an unbounded queue.join() that returns only once the
(daemon=False) event-bus worker has POSTed every scenario event to the
LangWatch endpoint; each POST has a 30s httpx timeout and the worker drains
serially. So teardown cost scales with event_count x up-to-30s whenever the
endpoint is reachable-but-slow. Multi-turn voice demos emit the most events
(one/turn + base64 audio snapshots) so their teardown is the most exposed;
several in one process compounds it past the 60s per-test timeout -> wedge.
Reproduced creds-free by pointing LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT at a socket that
accepts but never responds: the worker blocks in socket.recv_into while the
calling thread blocks in drain() -> queue.join(). Locally the default
endpoint fast-refuses, so the drain returns instantly — which is why the
wedge is invisible in isolation but bites in voice-integration.yml where
LANGWATCH_API_KEY is set. Full write-up in TESTING.md.

AC2 — resolution (creds-free path b): process-isolation, no skip papering.
- Remove the 6 @pytest.mark.skip markers on the multi-turn demos; tag them
  @pytest.mark.voice_multiturn (registered in pytest.ini) instead.
- voice-integration.yml deselects voice_multiturn from the two bulk
  single-process steps and runs each marked demo in its OWN pytest process
  (discovered by marker, so the set can't drift) — isolation neutralises the
  telemetry drain AND the documented adapter task/subprocess leaks at once.
- TESTING.md: replace the 'not yet isolated / run manually' note with the
  confirmed root cause + the supported marker mechanism; recommend a bounded
  event_bus.drain() as a separate SDK-wide follow-up.

* fix(voice/#498): surface recv-loop termination as attributable PipecatRecvError

The PipecatAgentAdapter 2nd-turn hang traced to a swallowed background-task
exit: when `_recv_loop` crashed (decode/transport error) or the bot closed the
WebSocket, the loop only logged a warning and the inbound queue went silent, so
the next `recv_audio` blocked the full `response_timeout` then raised an
empty-bodied `asyncio.TimeoutError` — hiding the real cause.

Diagnostic fix (the primary timeout's true cause is environment-specific and
cannot be reproduced creds-free in this worktree — see PR body):
- New generic `AgentStreamEndedError` (base adapter): a recv transport that
  TERMINATED, distinct from a transient `asyncio.TimeoutError`. `_drain` lets it
  propagate on the first chunk (names the real cause) and treats it as a normal
  end-of-turn on tail chunks.
- New `PipecatRecvError(AgentStreamEndedError)`: `_recv_loop` records a crash
  (no longer swallows) and a `finally` marks the loop done + enqueues a sentinel;
  `recv_audio` fails FAST with an attributable message, chaining the real crash
  via `__cause__` or naming the clean close.

This disambiguates the issue's hypotheses at the raise site: a dead loop now
fails loud (crash cause or "bot closed the WebSocket"), while a genuinely silent
agent still raises the existing `FirstChunkTimeoutError` (phase + timeout).

fix(judge): protect unbounded judge transcript for non-litellm agents (#837)

* fix(judge/#836): protect unbounded judge transcript for non-litellm agents

JudgeAgent's trace-size protection (structure-only digest + expand_trace/
grep_trace discovery) was gated entirely on JudgeSpanCollector spans, which
only ever contain spans from autotrack_litellm_calls. An AgentAdapter that
talks to its own backend directly (REST/SSE/etc., not via litellm) produces
tool-call messages that never become spans, so is_large_trace never tripped
for such agents while the raw `transcript` block built from input.messages
flowed into the judge prompt with no cap of any kind. A large enough
transcript could get "lost in the middle" for a small/cheap judge model,
producing a confident but wrong verdict instead of a visible failure.

Gate the transcript on its own estimated token count, independent of the
span digest. When it's large, render a structure-only skeleton (one line
per message: index, role, tool-call name, size) and offer the judge
expand_transcript/grep_transcript tools -- mirroring expand_trace/grep_trace
but keyed on message position instead of span ID -- so the full content is
still reachable on demand instead of force-fed on every call.

feat(sdk): reuse the LangWatch tab instead of opening one per run (#847)

* feat(sdk): reuse the LangWatch tab instead of opening one per run

Running a suite over and over, especially from a coding agent working in the
background, buried you in LangWatch tabs: one per batch, none of them ever
closing. Both SDKs now ask LangWatch whether a simulations tab from this
machine is still connected before opening anything. When one is, the run is
handed to it and no browser is opened; the tab moves itself to the new batch.

The machine is identified by a key in ~/.langwatch/scenario-tab-key, created
on first use and shared by both SDKs, so a tab opened by pytest is reused by
vitest. It rides along as a query param on the tab the SDK opens, and nothing
else.

Two fallbacks sit behind that. A LangWatch too old to answer the handoff gets a
time window instead: the same scenario set will not open a second tab within
SCENARIO_BROWSER_REOPEN_SECONDS. And SCENARIO_BROWSER (auto/never/always)
decides whether a browser may be opened at all, overriding SCENARIO_HEADLESS
and headless config so a tab can be forced open from an otherwise headless
setup. CI never opens one.

Every step fails open: a hanging handoff, an unwritable state directory or a
missing browser can only cost the tab, never the run.

* fix(sdk): make the browser launch survive a fast-exiting run

Dogfooding surfaced a case where the SDK reported a tab as opened and no tab
appeared. Two fire-and-forget hops were to blame, and both are now awaited.

`open()` only spawns its launcher a few ticks after it is called, so the old
`void open(url)` lost the tab whenever the process ended promptly afterwards.
The event bus had the same shape one level up: the watch message was handed to
an rxjs `tap`, which drops the promise, so the run could finish and the process
exit while the handoff request was still in flight.

The watch message now settles inside the existing concatMap stage. It fires
once per batch and is off the scenario's own critical path, so the ordering
costs nothing.

* fix(sdk): keep partial throttle state and make the tests platform-honest

Review follow-ups. A single malformed entry used to throw away the whole
throttle file, which would reopen a tab for every set; the Python reader now
skips just the bad entry, matching what the TypeScript one already did.

The 'unusable state directory' tests pinned a Linux-only /proc path, so on
other platforms they were passing through the success path for the wrong
reason. They now point the state directory inside a regular file, which no
platform will let anyone mkdir into.

* docs(scenario): document the browser tab and drop em dashes from new copy

* docs(scenario): describe the connected badge instead of the follow toast

The reused tab now follows runs silently and wears a Connected to local
run badge in the set header. The Stop following control is gone: a tab
that should stay put is one you open yourself, which never follows.

* docs(scenario): fold browser-tab reuse into the config table row

A dedicated section explaining tab reuse, the key file, and the reopen
window put a wall of prose above the config file docs for something the
table row can say in one line. The row description now carries what each
SCENARIO_BROWSER value does, so no further reading is needed to use it.

* docs(scenario): the throttle isn't just for old LangWatch instances

CodeRabbit caught it: an unreachable endpoint or a timeout hits the same
fallback as a 404 from an instance too old to answer. Widened the config
table row and both module docstrings to say so instead of naming only the
oldest cause.

* docs(scenario): stop enumerating throttle-fallback causes

Naming unreachable/timeout/too-old invites drift the next time a new
cause shows up. 'Can't confirm whether a tab is already open' covers
all of them without a list to maintain.

fix(voice): real voice-in on Python ElevenLabs, per-call personalisation, agent hangup, and corrected docs (#848)

* fix(voice): real voice-in on Python ElevenLabs, per-call personalisation, and graceful agent hangup

The Python hosted-ElevenLabs adapter defaulted to committing a user turn as
text: it sent `{"type":"user_message"}` and DISCARDED the audio, so the agent
under test never heard the caller and its STT and VAD never ran. A green run
proved nothing about either. Verified live against a real ConvAI agent: 0 speech
frames on the wire and 0 `user_transcript` events. The TypeScript adapter fixed
this in #707 and names the behaviour a regression; Python never got the port.

Default is now `turn_commit_mode="audio"`: the turn's real PCM is streamed as
20 ms frames at microphone cadence, then unbounded closing silence, which is the
audio→silence transition ElevenLabs' server VAD closes a turn on. Live after:
376 speech frames and ElevenLabs' own transcription of our audio on every turn.
`"text"` and `"silence"` remain as opt-in escape hatches.

Also in this change:

- `dynamic_variables` and deep-merged `overrides` on the Python adapter, closing
  the gap with the TypeScript twin (#838). Production integrations personalise a
  deployed agent per call this way rather than overriding the prompt, which on
  ElevenLabs replaces the entire prompt object including `tool_ids` and silently
  strips a hosted agent's tools. Documented with that warning.

- An agent-initiated hangup ends the scenario gracefully in both SDKs (#839).
  Hosted agents routinely invoke `end_call` after their farewell, closing the
  socket; a leftover scripted turn then failed a run in which the agent behaved
  exactly as designed. The adapters now recognise the `agent_tool_response` frame
  ElevenLabs emits for a successful hangup or transfer tool, expose it as
  `agent_hung_up` / `agentHungUp`, and conclude rather than raising. An
  unsuccessful tool, or a close with no hangup, still raises as before.

- Docs corrected. `troubleshooting.mdx` and `recipes/multi-turn.mdx` claimed
  hosted ElevenLabs supported only a single greeting-led exchange and routed
  multi-turn users to a different adapter. That has been false since #596/#707
  and would have steered an ElevenLabs customer off the adapter built for them.
  The same claim was baked into `getting-started.mdx` and into the
  voice-elevenlabs-hosted-e2e spec's Background, which is rewritten around the
  behaviour that actually ships.

- `happy-path-elevenlabs.mdx` gains TypeScript tabs; it was Python-only, so a
  TypeScript reader landed on the better-supported path and saw none of it. Every
  documented snippet was compiled against the real API.

- The CI test agent now allowlists `agent.language` so the overrides path is
  exercisable end to end.

Verified live against a real ElevenLabs ConvAI agent, not mocks: real-audio
multi-turn with ElevenLabs transcribing each turn, a dynamic variable plus a
Spanish language override surviving one handshake together, and a scripted turn
after an `end_call` concluding cleanly.

* fix(voice/python): attribute stranded agent audio at the turn boundary (#749)

The drain closes an agent turn on `response_tail_silence`. ElevenLabs delivers
audio in bursts, so a mid-utterance delivery gap longer than that silence ended
the turn while the agent was still speaking, and the remainder was read by the
NEXT drain as that turn's opening audio. Turn N+1 then appears to answer
question N.

Caught live rather than by inspection: a two-turn hosted run where the agent's
reply to "can you tell me your support hours?" was its reply to the previous
question, which the judge correctly failed. Intermittent, roughly one run in
three, because it depends on where the delivery gap falls.

TypeScript fixed this in #748 by reconciling its buffered audio queue at the
user-turn boundary. Python reads the socket directly and has no such queue, which
is why the port was never a straight copy. The equivalent safe point is the same
one: pre-user-`send_audio`, before the user segment is written. At that instant
the agent cannot have begun its next reply, so anything still arriving is
unambiguously the prior turn's tail, and an agent segment is still last on the
cursor.

`reconcile_pending_audio` sweeps up what is in flight, bounded by a short
wall-clock budget so a turn boundary never stalls on a slow agent. Attribution is
position-gated exactly as in TypeScript: cursor-safe grows the preceding agent
segment and clears its transcript so the finalize STT back-fill re-transcribes
the now-longer audio; cursor-unsafe (no recording, the opening greeting, or a
barge-in where a user segment is last) drops it with a warning rather than
corrupting the append-only cursor. Either way the audio is off the wire, so it
can no longer bleed.

The recovery path warns and points at `response_tail_silence`, so an agent whose
delivery is consistently gappier than the default is visible rather than silently
patched over. Documented on the adapter page.

Adapters that expose no `reconcile_pending_audio` are untouched by the duck-typed
hook, matching the existing `last_agent_transcript` convention.

* fix(voice/python): preserve the reconciled segment's transcript and keep the sweep out of turn latency

Two defects in the turn-boundary reconcile, caught reviewing the diff.

Clearing `prior.transcript` was wrong on both counts. The early close cuts the
turn in AUDIO only — ElevenLabs' `agent_response` text already covers the whole
utterance — so the transcript was correct and appending the tail is what makes
the two consistent. Clearing it also assumed the STT back-fill would regenerate
one, but `transcribe_segments` runs only when the judge model cannot ingest
audio; an audio-capable judge (the common case for voice) would have left the
segment with no transcript at all.

The sweep also ran inside the window measured for `voice.turn.latency_ms`, so a
turn was billed for time spent draining the PREVIOUS turn — up to the full
reconcile budget of inflation on every scripted user turn, in a metric people
use for perf assertions. The start is now re-stamped once the sweep completes.

* docs(voice): name the likely cause in the reconcile drop warning

The drop branch fires when there is no preceding agent segment, which in
practice almost always means the script did not lead with agent() and the
on-connect greeting arrived after the first user turn was queued. Say so, so the
warning points at the fix instead of just reporting a byte count.

* docs(voice): drop code-group tab labels from standalone fences

Two fences outside any :::code-group carried a [python] tab label, which only
means something inside a group.

* docs(spec): retitle the keepalive live AC now that the hosted test is multi-turn

AC-KA4 called its subject the "live single-exchange happy path", but the test it
names (elevenlabs-hosted.test.ts) scripts two user turns. The AC itself is
unchanged — only the label described a shape the test no longer has.

* fix(voice): address CodeRabbit review on #848

`agent_hung_up` was instance-only, which broke the base adapter's stated
contract that a subclass may skip `super().__init__()` — the same reason
`_voice_turn_context` carries a class-level default and `_agent_speaking_event`
has a lazy safety net. Such an adapter would have hit AttributeError from the
`call()` gate instead of the intended TransportNotConnectedError. Now a
class-level default, matching the TS field default.

The TypeScript quick start installed only `@langwatch/scenario` and then ran
vitest, which the reader does not have. Now installs vitest explicitly and uses
pnpm for install and CI, matching introduction/getting-started.mdx.

Also from the review: annotate `reconcile_prior_agent_audio`'s parameters; give
the `# type: ignore[arg-type]` its required explanation; point AC-KA4 at the real
test path (`javascript/examples/vitest/tests/...`, which is where that test
actually lives); and retag the adapter-page docs assertion `@integration` since
it gates documentation, not code.

The reconcile test named "no recording" was passing an executor that had an empty
one, leaving the genuine `recording is None` branch uncovered. Split into three:
empty recording, an executor with no `_voice_recording` at all, and a null
executor (the shape `_AdapterRecorder` degrades to on lightweight test stubs).

* chore(voice): clear the remaining CodeRabbit nitpicks

Mark the reconcile's deliberate best-effort catch with the BLE001 noqa the
codebase uses elsewhere for the same pattern, and drop the _speech_frames test
helper I added and then never used.

* fix(voice/python): keep reconcile_prior_agent_audio's parameters duck-typed

Annotating `adapter` as `VoiceAgentAdapter` broke `pyright .` on the two tests
that deliberately pass bare doubles to prove the hook is duck-typed. The
annotation described a contract the function does not enforce: it feature-detects
`reconcile_pending_audio` via getattr rather than requiring the base class, and
reads the recording off the executor the same way. Both are `Any`, with the

OPENAI_API_KEY in CI now holds a LangWatch virtual key, with

refactor(execution): consolidate the two next-agent-for-role lookups (#210) (#860)

`nextAgentForRole` and `getNextAgentForRole` answered the same question with
different return shapes, and differed by one extra condition:
`pendingRolesOnTurn.includes(role)`, present on the former and absent on the
latter. They are now one `findNextAgentForRole` returning the single
`{ index, agent } | null` shape.

The condition is dropped, which is behaviour-preserving because it cannot be
false at any of the three call sites that had it:

- `_step` passes `pendingRolesOnTurn[0]`, so it asks whether an array contains
  its own head. On an empty queue the role is `undefined` and no agent matches
  on role either way.
- The inline-barge lookup iterates `for (const r of pendingRolesOnTurn)`, and
  its second call asks for AGENT only after `nextRole` was assigned from that
  same iteration, with nothing mutating the array in between.

Keeping the condition instead would NOT have been behaviour-preserving: it
would have added it to the scripted path, where its absence is load-bearing.
`scriptCallAgent` runs `consumeUntilRole` first, which drains the queue
entirely when the role is not in it, and the agent has to stay reachable after
that. Python's `_next_agent_for_role` does keep the condition and so takes a
`newTurn()` there instead, making this a real turn-count divergence rather than
a tidy-up. It is pinned here, not changed: aligning the two languages is a
behaviour decision for the parity question on the issue.

Nothing observed any of this before. Restoring the condition for all call sites
left all 1079 existing JS tests green while moving `currentTurn` from 0 to 1
after a scripted `agent()` then `user()`. The new
`script-call-role-pending.test.ts` reaches that state through the public API and
fails on exactly that mutation.

1081 tests pass (1079 plus these 2), typecheck and lint:lib clean.

Closes #210

feat: judge fetches remote traces with per-turn trace propagation (#909)

* feat(python): fetch remote traces for judge evaluation

AgentInput gains propagation_headers, the W3C trace context of the
current turn, built at call time so HTTP adapters can forward it to the
agent under test. New fetch_remote_traces and trace_wait_timeout options
on ScenarioConfig, scenario.configure() and scenario.run() make the
judge fetch the traces the agent reported to LangWatch and merge them
into its digest before the verdict.

Mid-conversation judge calls never wait: one non-blocking fetch round.
A required verdict settle-waits, polling every second under the shared
timeout, until the trace is complete: at least one remote span and
every fetched span's parent resolved. At the deadline the judge keeps
every fetched span and the digest gains a synthetic
langwatch.span_collection.error span saying whether no agent spans
arrived or the trace is still incomplete; the judge rule reads that
reason and keeps unproven criteria inconclusive, never passed on
transcript claims alone. A voluntary finish_test completes trace
collection and is re-issued exactly once with the full digest, and the
second verdict wins.

* feat(javascript): fetch remote traces for judge evaluation

AgentInput gains optional propagationHeaders, the W3C trace context of
the current turn, always set by the scenario runtime at call time and
optional on the interface so hand-built inputs keep compiling. New
fetchRemoteTraces and traceWaitTimeoutMs options on ScenarioConfig and
the scenario.config.js project config make the judge fetch the traces
the agent reported to LangWatch and merge them into its digest before
the verdict.

Same contract as the Python SDK: no wait mid-conversation; at verdict a
settle-wait polls every second under the shared timeout until the trace
is complete, meaning at least one remote span and every fetched span's
parent resolved; at the deadline the judge keeps every fetched span
plus a synthetic langwatch.span_collection.error span whose reason the
judge rule reads; a voluntary finish_test completes trace collection
and is re-issued exactly once with the full digest, and the second
verdict wins.

* docs: remote traces guide and integration updates

New advanced/remote-traces page: trace propagation, the config options,
the settle-wait behavior and failure handling, with one runnable example
per language. How Judging Works documents the remote fetch stage, the
two-phase voluntary verdict and the judge rule verbatim. The HTTPS
integration and blackbox testing guides forward the propagation headers,
configuration lists the new options with defaults, and ADR-006 plus the
feature spec record the decision.

* feat(python): two-phase judge with settle-wait retry and terminal no-evidence verdicts

The judge splits into a decision call (argument-free continue_test and
make_verdict, no remote fetching, skipped below the min_turns floor) and
a dedicated verdict call that settle-waits once with finish_test pinned.
A failed poll retries until the deadline instead of failing the trace,
and each request carries a fixed 30 second bound. A voluntary
inconclusive verdict stays non-terminal, except when no trace of the run
ever settled: more turns cannot produce the missing evidence.

* feat(javascript): two-phase judge with settle-wait retry and terminal no-evidence verdicts

Same split as the Python SDK: an argument-free decision call and a
dedicated verdict call that settle-waits once. Failed polls retry until
the deadline, each request has a fixed 30 second bound (the wait budget
no longer feeds AbortSignal.timeout a fractional remainder), and a
voluntary inconclusive verdict is terminal when no trace ever settled.

* docs: two-phase judge semantics in ADR and guides

* fix: review feedback on span attribute parity and test input merging

The TypeScript API span converter now writes langwatch.input /
langwatch.output with the same serialization as the Python SDK, so the
judge digest reads the same whichever SDK fetched the trace. The
two-phase test input helper merges overrides before the nested defaults,
and the propagation example drops an unused import.

* feat(python): process-span registry, 30s wait default, judge wait_for_traces extension

The judge span collector registers every span this process starts
(on_start), and the remote trace fetcher uses that registry to recognize
platform echoes: spans the scenario itself produced never count as
remote evidence, so a trace that holds only echoes now reports 'no agent
spans arrived' instead of 'still incomplete'. Fixes #910.

The default trace wait budget drops from 60 to 30 seconds. When the
settle-wait ends with incomplete traces, the verdict call offers a
one-shot wait_for_traces tool: calling it re-arms the failed traces,
retracts their synthetic error spans, and settle-waits once more under
trace_wait_extension (default: the wait budget). The tool is then
withdrawn and the judge must deliver its verdict.

* feat(javascript): process-span registry, 30s wait default, judge wait_for_traces extension

Mirrors the Python change: the judge span collector registers every span
this process starts (onStart) and the fetcher treats those ids as
platform echoes, never remote evidence. Fixes #910 for this SDK too.

DEFAULT_TRACE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS drops from 60000 to 30000, settleWait
reports whether every trace settled, and the verdict call offers the
one-shot wait_for_traces tool backed by extendSettle under
traceWaitExtensionMs (default: the resolved wait budget).

* docs: 30s wait default, wait_for_traces extension, process-span echo registry

* fix: review feedback on fetch bounds, budget guards and registry cleanup

A trace API request is now bounded by whichever is nearer, the fixed 30
second request guard or what is left of the settle loop's shared
deadline, and the bound covers the response body read. The abort raises
a deadline sentinel the settle loop recognises, so a run that ran out of
time reports what arrived instead of a fetch that kept failing. The
fetch sends X-Project-Id when a project id is configured, which the
platform's bearer branch requires for organization and personal keys.

Wait budgets that are not finite positive numbers are rejected: the
pydantic fields gain allow_inf_nan=False and the JS judge drops them
with a warning, falling back to the next source. The forced verdict
offers finish_test only in both SDKs, closing the same deny-list leak
for wait_for_traces that the pin alone does not close.

The process-span registry releases a thread's traces when the run
completes: the settle-wait claims every trace id it touches, and the
collector's per-thread clear drops the claims, covering traces whose
local echoes never end or never carry the thread id.

The hanging-fetch test asserted only that the reason names the timeout. It

The forced-verdict test annotates its capture dict and its completion stub,

DEFAULT_TRACE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0, and the PR description says 30,
so the API reference contradicted both.

Also close the check-then-act in RemoteTraceFetcher._state. The lock was
taken to fetch the per-thread dict and released before the membership test,
so two callers could both miss and both create, and the loser's state
object would be dropped while its caller still held a reference. One lock
now covers both steps.

ci: make two workflow-validator checks able to fail (#903) (#911)

* ci: make two workflow-validator checks able to fail (#903)

The path-filter assertion grepped the whole workflow for a substring, so
any line carrying the needle satisfied it. For docs-ci two unrelated
lines do, the sibling filter entry and the build job's
cache-dependency-path, so deleting the real filter still reported PASS.
It now reads the relevant list the detect-changes step declares, the way
every other check in that script already parses the YAML.

The auto-approve validator checked that the workflow references the
policy document and that the reference is canonical, but never that the
document is there. Deleting it left every check green over a workflow
that cats a missing path.

Closes #903

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: tighten both new guards to match what they claim

The detect-changes step is matched by exact reference: an action whose
name merely contains "detect-changes" could supply a filters input and
satisfy the check without the job using the local one, which is the same
shape of hole this change was written to close.

The policy-document check uses -s rather than -f, matching the workflow,
which already refuses an empty policy at run time. Accepting one would
have reported green over a state the workflow rejects.

test(voice): resolve the feature path once instead of in 22 suites (#521) (#881)

* test(voice): resolve the feature path once instead of in 22 suites (#521)

Every cucumber-bound suite counted its own hops back to the repository root to
reach specs/voice-agents.feature. The count depends on how deep the suite sits,
so src/voice/__tests__ needed four and src/agents/judge/__tests__ needed five,
and 22 files each carried an answer that is only correct where they happen to
live. Moving a test file breaks its path silently; moving specs/ means finding
all 22.

Anchors the resolution on one module instead, so the depth is a property of a
single file. The helper also names a missing spec, because loadFeature fails on
one with a parse error quoting a path nobody wrote.

The ticket counted four such files. It is 22 now, which is the argument for
doing it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(voice): compare path segments instead of a posix substring

The guard that the feature path escapes the javascript package matched the
literal "/javascript/", which never appears on Windows because path.resolve
separates with a backslash there. Split on the platform separator instead, so
the assertion means the same thing wherever it runs.

process() unpacked every incoming byte into a number[] one push at a
time, then took each frame with slice() and dropped it with
splice(0, BYTES_PER_FRAME), which shifts the whole remainder once per
frame. The source is already a Uint8Array, so the unpack was a scatter
copy fighting the typed-array model.

Frames are now subarray views onto a Uint8Array, and the remainder is
compacted once per process() call rather than once per frame.

60 seconds of 24 kHz audio in 20 ms chunks, median of 7 runs:
18.2 ms before, 3.3 ms after.

The framing behaviour had no direct coverage, so it is pinned first: ten
tests written against the number[] implementation, passing unchanged
against this one.

Closes #525
