perf(js): load the ElevenLabs SDK only when voice runs (#933)

* perf(js): load the ElevenLabs SDK only when voice runs

A plain `import "@langwatch/scenario"` pulled 6,144 modules and 237MB
of RSS, and 4,972 of those modules were ElevenLabs. Every consumer paid
it, including a text-only scenario in a server that never does voice,
because index.ts re-exports the voice namespace and the three ElevenLabs
leaves imported the SDK at module scope.

The SDK now has one seam, voice/elevenlabs-sdk.ts, which imports it
inside a function body and exposes structural views of the parts we
call. Nothing else names it, so it reaches neither the module graph nor
the published declarations until a run actually does speech.

Same tree, before and after: 1,495ms -> 405ms, 6,144 -> 1,172 modules,
+237MB -> +89MB RSS, 4,972 -> 0 ElevenLabs modules. dist/index.d.ts no
longer imports the SDK, which also drops 2,605 declaration files from
every consumer's typecheck.

No API change: clientFactory still takes an injected client, and the
adapter's webSocketFactory and conversationClient still pass through.

* fix(js): make the SDK-import guard complete, and type the lazy boundary

The guard used .test() on a g-flagged regex, so lastIndex carried between
files and every second offender was skipped, and it matched only the
`from` form, missing a bare side-effect import. It now scans with
matchAll over two patterns, and excludes ';', '(' and ')' so a multi-line
named import still matches while a dynamic import inside a call does not.
Checked against nine forms, including two consecutive offenders.

The pass-through seams get real structural types instead of `object`, and
the loaded runtime a named module interface instead of `any`, so an
injected websocket factory or conversation client is still checked
without the SDK entering the published declarations.

* fix(js): give the realtime demo the zod its agents SDK needs

examples/openai-realtime-demo declared @openai/agents but no zod, so
pnpm resolved it against the zod 3 the SDK pins, while examples/vitest,
which imports the demo's agent, resolved the zod 4 build. Importing
@openai/agents/realtime from the zod 3 build throws at module scope
building a discriminated union, so tests/scenario-expert-realtime.test.ts
failed before it ran a single test. It fails the same way on main.

Declaring zod 4 in the demo lines both up on one instance. Verified by
importing @openai/agents/realtime under each build: zod 3.25.76 throws,
zod 4.4.3 imports. The example suite is now 40 passed, 0 failed, and the
realtime test passes end to end against a live key.

ci: document the gateway key handling, and record what blocks the Gemini lane (#908)

* ci(python): send the Gemini examples through the AI Gateway too

The OpenAI-shaped calls in this job have gone through the gateway since
July. The Gemini examples did not: litellm's gemini lane reads its own
base URL, so it kept calling Google directly with a raw provider key.

litellm builds `{GEMINI_API_BASE}/models/{model}:generateContent` and
sends the key as x-goog-api-key. Pointing GEMINI_API_BASE at the
gateway's /v1beta surface therefore needs no change to any example: the
same virtual key already in OPENAI_API_KEY serves both lanes.

The whole examples suite was run against a locally built gateway with
one virtual key covering both lanes: 27 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.

voice-integration.yml keeps its direct Google key. Gemini Live is a
websocket API the gateway does not proxy.

The header now records how to rotate, revoke and cap the key, and how to
put the provider keys back, which the file assumed but never said.

* docs(ci): correct the gateway key notes and record the websocket exception

Review follow-ups.

The budget note described the refusal loosely. The gateway answers a hard
breach with HTTP 402 `budget_exceeded` and puts the scope in
`error.meta.budget_scope`; this key's cap is virtual-key scoped, daily,
and now $10. The note carries the numbers that justify that size: one
full run costs about $0.09 and the busiest day seen was 31 runs.

The revoke note implied revocation is instant. Each gateway pod caches a
key's config for 60 seconds, so a revoked secret can keep working for
about a minute unless the deployment is restarted.

javascript-ci needed no routing change, which was worth saying rather
than leaving the reader to compare two files: its traffic has gone
through the gateway since #848, and both client families the examples
use read OPENAI_BASE_URL. Its header now names them, points at the key
notes in python-ci.yml instead of copying them, and states why OpenAI
Realtime still holds a direct key: it opens a websocket, and the gateway
proxies HTTP only.

* ci(python): keep the Gemini examples on the direct key, and say why

Probing the production gateway before merging this showed the routing
would have gone red. The LangWatch organization has no Gemini provider
configured, so nothing on the gateway can serve a Gemini request.

The same virtual key, at the same moment, on the production gateway:

  /v1/chat/completions  gemini/gemini-2.5-flash
    400 model_provider_not_bound, "no gemini provider is configured"

  /v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent
    404, meta.provider = anthropic

The first is correct. The second is langwatch/langwatch#7035 on
production: the same missing credential, and the passthrough surface
sent the prompt to Anthropic instead of refusing.

So the two routing lines come out and the step keeps the direct Google
key. The mechanism itself is measured and works: the whole examples
suite passes through a gateway that does hold a Google credential, 27

exactly which one and what to swap when it exists.

* docs(ci): adding the Gemini provider is two steps, not one

The note said to add a Gemini provider to the organization and swap the
two lines. That is not enough on its own. eligibleModelProvidersForVk in
scopeResolver.ts maps a pinned key's chain from the routing policy's

The note now names both steps and points at `GET /v1/models` on the key
as the check, since that lists what the key can actually dispatch to.

feat(voice): let the realtime adapters mint through a voice gateway (#935)

* feat(voice): let the realtime adapters mint through a voice gateway

A voice gateway can broker a realtime session rather than relay it: the
client presents a virtual key, the gateway checks the budget and the
open-session cap and mints the vendor's own short-lived credential, and the
media socket still runs client to vendor. Audio never crosses the gateway, so
latency and the wire protocol are unchanged, and the call lands on one spend
record.

Until now neither realtime adapter could reach one. ElevenLabs built its SDK
client with no way to set a base URL, and the OpenAI Realtime adapter dialled
a hardcoded endpoint with a long-lived provider key and had no mint step at
all. So a deployment that put a virtual key in OPENAI_API_KEY had to keep a
real provider key in OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY for voice to work, which routed
voice around the gateway that was supposed to be measuring it.

ElevenLabs takes a `baseUrl`, passed straight to the SDK client, because the
gateway mirrors the vendor's own signed-URL path. OpenAI takes a `broker`:
the adapter mints through POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets, dials with the
ephemeral secret the gateway returns, and posts what the socket measured to
POST /v1/realtime/sessions/{id}/usage when the session ends. Usage is read
off response.done in the raw message path, because a drain that ends on tail
silence never reads the terminal event and an unreported session bills as
cost-unknown.

Brokering is opt-in and off by default. With no broker configured both
adapters connect exactly as before, byte for byte, and OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY
keeps working for deployments that rely on it. A brokered adapter never reads
that variable: it holds a direct provider key, so minting with it would
present a credential the gateway cannot bill.

REALTIME_URL_TEMPLATE is no longer a fixed constant. The endpoint resolves
from an explicit option, then OPENAI_REALTIME_URL, then the vendor default.

* refactor(voice): mint through the vendors' own configuration

The adapters read no LangWatch-specific variable. OpenAI Realtime mints at
${OPENAI_BASE_URL}/realtime/client_secrets with OPENAI_API_KEY, the two
variables scenario already reads for chat. That path is OpenAI's own and the
AI Gateway mirrors it, so the same request works against either: point it at
OpenAI and the vendor mints, point it at a gateway and the gateway checks the
budget and the open-session cap and opens a spend record. Anyone already
routing chat through a gateway gets voice with no new configuration.

The adapter learns which one answered from the response, not from a flag: a
gateway returns X-LangWatch-Session-Id and the vendor does not, so usage is
reported back only when there is a session to report to.

A base URL with no mint route answers 404. That is an absence, so the adapter
dials the vendor directly with OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY and warns, because an
unbilled run must not read as a billed one. A refusal such as an exhausted
budget raises instead, so a declined call cannot run on a direct provider key.

ElevenLabs keeps the SDK's own baseUrl option and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. The SDK
reads no base URL variable, so there is none to follow.

* test(voice): let the ElevenLabs demo read a base URL from the environment

The OpenAI demo already runs against a gateway with no code change, because
the adapter reads OPENAI_BASE_URL. The ElevenLabs SDK reads no base URL
variable of its own, so the demo reads one itself and passes it to the SDK's
baseUrl option. Unset, the SDK talks to ElevenLabs directly as before.

* fix(voice): treat a refused or stalled usage report as a failure

A non-2xx answer was read as a report that landed. A 404 for an unknown
session or a 401 for a rotated key would leave the session to settle as
cost-unknown with nobody told why, so the response status is now checked and
onError is called on it.

The request is also bounded. disconnect() awaits the report, so an unbounded
request held the websocket open and the test that owned it never finished.

The direct-dial warning now names the variable the key actually came from.
The adapter reads three in order, so naming a fixed one sent the reader to a
variable that is not set.

Also restores the console.warn spy in the mint test: vi.unstubAllGlobals does
not undo vi.spyOn, so a silenced logger outlived the file.

* fix(voice): check the ElevenLabs base URL at construction

A base URL that includes /v1 produces /v1/v1/convai/... and a 404 that names
no cause. It is the mistake to expect, because OPENAI_BASE_URL conventionally
does include /v1 and the ElevenLabs SDK appends its own. It cost a real
debugging round, so the constructor now refuses it and says what the request
would have become. A value that is not a URL is refused there too, and an
empty one still means unset.

* fix(voice): bound the mint, and close a session whose socket never opened

connect() waits for the mint before it opens the socket, so an unbounded
request left connection setup pending forever against a stalled endpoint. The
mint now carries an abort timeout, the same way the usage report already did.
The report was bounded first and the mint was missed, which is the adjacent
branch of one condition.

A mint that succeeded followed by a socket that failed to open left the
session open at the gateway. disconnect() returns early when there is no
socket, so nothing ever reported against it, and it held one of the key's
open-session slots until the gateway's window expired while booking a call
that never happened. The failure path now closes it with a zero usage report.
Zero is the truth rather than a placeholder: an ephemeral credential that
opened no socket consumed nothing at the vendor.

* fix(voice): restrict the ElevenLabs base URL to http and https

new URL parses schemes the SDK cannot make a REST request over, so parsing
alone was not a check.

* test(voice): cover the base URL reaching the ElevenLabs client

Normalizing a value the adapter never passes on would be a check with no
effect, so the SDK runtime is stubbed and the client's own option bag is
asserted. The omission case reads the keys rather than comparing objects,
because toEqual treats an undefined property as absent and would pass on
`baseUrl: undefined`, which is the one thing that case rules out.

ci(python): give fork PRs something that reads the examples they change (#893) (#932)

* ci(python): give fork PRs something that reads the examples they change

The examples suite needs repo secrets, so it is skipped on fork and
Dependabot PRs, and the aggregator counts the skipped step's job as a
success. An examples-only change from an external contributor therefore
reached a green required check with nothing having imported the file it
changed.

Collection imports every example module and makes no provider call, so
it runs where the live suite cannot. One resolver step decides whether
secrets are readable and both example steps gate on it, so exactly one
of them runs. A check in validate-aggregator-workflows.sh pins that.

Refs #893

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(python): pin what each examples step does, not just that two exist

The check accepted any resolver that wrote something to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
so one writing a different name passed while `available` stayed empty,
which turns the live suite off everywhere and the collection on. It also
never checked that the secret-enabled step runs the suite, so that step
could become a second collect-only run with both gates still correct.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(python): run the resolver to check it, instead of reading it

Matching strings in the resolver's shell cannot answer the question the
check is asking. A substring matches a commented-out line, and whether
two writes are mutually exclusive is control flow, not text.

The validator now extracts the resolver and runs it across every event
shape the workflow can see, asserting the value a later step would read.
That catches an inverted condition and an unconditional pair of writes,
neither of which any string match sees. The two example commands are
matched as commands on executable lines, so a narrowed path or a
commented-out one no longer passes.

feat(voice): mint every JavaScript voice session through the gateway (#937)

* feat(voice): mint every JavaScript voice session through the gateway

RealtimeAgentAdapter, the @openai/agents lane, dialled OpenAI with a
long-lived key and never minted. It is the lane the failing example test
uses, and its key was dead, so javascript-ci was red.

It now calls the same broker OpenAIRealtimeAgentAdapter uses. The
mint-or-dial rule moves into one function, acquireRealtimeSocketKey, so
the two adapters cannot disagree about it: a mint answers and the socket
carries the ephemeral secret; a 404 means the base URL is not a gateway,
so the vendor is dialled with a warning; any other error status is a
refusal and raises without opening a socket.

ElevenLabs ConvAI rides the gateway too. The hosted adapter reads
ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL and ELEVENLABS_CONVAI_API_KEY itself, so the seven
demos that built one no longer repeat the wiring. The gateway fronts the
ConvAI mint route only, so the speech-to-text and text-to-speech leaves
take an explicit baseUrl and keep the vendor key.

OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY leaves both JavaScript workflows. With no
provider key in the job there is nothing to fall back to, which is how
the Python lane already proves its own routing.

* docs(ci): correct the gateway key's daily cap and say what shares it

The cap was documented as $10 and was $4. A javascript-voice-integration
run breached it mid-suite: the voice workflows share this virtual key and
cost far more per run than python-ci, because the realtime and ElevenLabs
sessions are minted through the gateway too. Raised to $15.

* fix(voice): mint for the connect model, and let a gateway-only setup run

Four review findings.

The mint used the session's model even when connect({ model }) named
another. The socket opens with the connect model, so the gateway priced
and budgeted a session the call never used. It now mints for whichever
model connect will actually pass.

An empty explicit baseUrl or apiKey suppressed the environment instead
of falling through to it. Empty is what an absent variable spreads into
an options object as, so both resolvers now treat it as unset.

The seven hosted demos gated on ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, so a gateway-only
setup holding only ELEVENLABS_CONVAI_API_KEY skipped every one of them.
They ask resolveElevenLabsConvAIApiKey instead, which is the same
function the adapter uses, so the gate cannot drift from the rule. The
branded demo keeps the vendor key, because its lane still talks to
ElevenLabs.

Import order in the new test file.

* fix(voice): skip a blank ElevenLabs key, and name the workflows on the cap

A variable set to a stray space is truthy, so it would be presented as
the credential and fail the mint with a 401 that names no cause. Every
candidate is trimmed before it is chosen.

The cap note said "the voice-integration workflows" share the key. Only
javascript-ci and javascript-voice-integration mint through the gateway.
voice-integration.yml, the Python one, still dials both vendors directly,
so its voice traffic does not land on this budget.

* fix(voice): bill a realtime session for every turn, and close an idle one

Two defects the Python side found by probing the live vendor, both present
in the TypeScript.

A multi-turn session billed for its last turn only. _captureUsage replaced
the running total on every response.done, and its comment claimed the last
response carried a session total. It does not. Measured on the live
Realtime API through the gateway: two turns reported input=9 output=4 then
input=22 output=4. Cumulative would have been output=8. So a ten-turn call
reported one turn, which is worse than reporting nothing, because an
unreported session settles as cost-unknown at the gateway's grace while a
wrong report arrives looking authoritative. Every numeric leaf is now
summed, recursing into the token detail objects a gateway prices
separately.

A session that opened no socket was closed with usage {}, which the
gateway refuses with HTTP 400 because it reads a report by looking for
input_tokens or output_tokens. The refusal went into a debug log, so the
record stayed open holding one of the key's slots. Measured: {} answers
400, {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0} answers 202. A brokered mint now
starts the total at stated zeros, which also closes a session that
connects and disconnects with no response at all, and made
_closeUnusedSession unnecessary, so it is gone and the socket-open failure
path calls the same report the normal path does.

RealtimeAgentAdapter had the second defect in a harder form: it minted and
never reported at all, so every session it opened held a slot. It now taps
the SDK's raw transport event and reports the same accumulated total.

The refusal message matches the Python wording so the two SDKs read alike.

* fix(voice): close a minted session whose @openai/agents socket never opens

The mint books a gateway session before session.connect() runs. A rejected
connect rethrew without reporting, so the record stayed open holding one of
the key's slots until the gateway's grace expired. The failure path now
calls the same report the normal path does, and the total is still the
zeros the mint seeded, which is the truth for a socket that never opened.
OpenAIRealtimeAgentAdapter already did this; the two now match.

The freshness test for zeroRealtimeUsage proved nothing, because the
accumulator returns a new object and left its input untouched either way.
It now mutates one zero and asserts the next is unaffected.

feat(voice): let the python realtime adapters mint through a voice gateway (#938)

* feat(voice): let the python realtime adapters mint through a voice gateway

A voice gateway can broker a realtime session rather than relay it: the
client presents a virtual key, the gateway checks the budget and the
open-session cap and mints the vendor's own short-lived credential, and the
media socket still runs client to vendor. Audio never crosses the gateway, so
latency and the wire protocol are unchanged, and the call lands on one spend
record.

Until now neither Python realtime adapter could reach one. The OpenAI Realtime
adapter dialled a hardcoded endpoint with a long-lived provider key from
OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY and had no mint step at all, and the ElevenLabs adapter
dialled the vendor websocket with a raw xi-api-key. So the one part of the
voice suite that spends the most money was the one part the gateway could not
meter.

This is the Python port of scenario#935, which did the same for TypeScript.
The new scenario/voice/broker.py keeps the same semantics: brokering is
configured vendor-natively, with no bespoke broker URL or broker key, and
brokered-ness is read off the X-LangWatch-Session-Id response header rather
than from a flag.

A refused mint can no longer be dialled around. 404 means the base URL has no
mint route, which is a plain proxy or an older gateway, so the adapter falls
back to a direct dial and warns. Every other error status belongs to an
endpoint that has the route and declined to use it: a rejected key, an
exhausted budget, a session cap, an outage. Those raise, and the message names
the status and says the gateway refused. Falling back there would run exactly
the call the gateway declined to bill.

voice-integration no longer carries OPENAI_REALTIME_API_KEY. With no provider
key in the job there is nothing to fall back to, so a run that reached OpenAI
directly cannot pass. Its pytest steps also turn the fallback warning into a
test failure, so a job can only go green if every voice session was minted.

* fix(examples): stop the two live-judge examples failing python-ci

The Test (Examples) step has been red on every push since 2026-08-20, on a
rotating pair drawn from three examples. Both causes are real, and neither is
judge noise.

test_lovable_clone failed on the same criterion five times out of five: "agent
modified the index.css file, not only the Index.tsx file". The agent's system
prompt told it to "start by the src/index.css and tailwind.config.ts files",
with no verb, so the model read them and moved on. The prompt now says to
update src/index.css, which is what the criterion has always described and
what a site builder of this kind does.

test_running_in_parallel::test_user_is_hungry let the user simulator drive
three free-form follow-up turns. It wandered into asking for meat, the agent's
hard rule made it decline, and the judge then failed the three criteria that
ask for an actual recipe. Its sibling in test_running_in_parallel_with_arun
already fixed this with fixed follow-up strings and two agent turns, and it
passes. That shape is now used in both files.

Four tests carried @pytest.mark.flaky under @pytest.mark.asyncio_concurrent,
which does nothing. pytest-asyncio-concurrent runs a group from its own
protocol hook, and pytest-rerunfailures implements reruns in
pytest_runtest_protocol, which that hook never calls. It emits no warning and
the summary counts no reruns, so a test declared to survive four attempts was
reported as a hard failure on its first. The dead markers are gone and a
collection guard in python/conftest.py refuses the combination, so it cannot
come back silently.

Verified with three consecutive green local runs of all five tests in the two
parallel example files plus test_lovable_clone.

* test(voice): assert a gateway answered the realtime mint

Every other proof of routing in the voice job is an argument about what did
not happen: there is no provider key to fall back to, and a direct-dial
fallback is promoted to a test failure. This asserts what did happen. A
gateway names the session it opened on X-LangWatch-Session-Id and the vendor
does not, so the header is the one thing that cannot be told a lie about what
answered, and the id it carries is the spend record the mint opened.

No media socket is opened. The mint alone proves the route, and the session it
books is closed at once with a zero usage report, which is the truth for a
credential that opened no socket.

* fix(voice): let a cancelled usage report cancel its task

report_openai_realtime_usage caught BaseException so it could return the
failure instead of raising it. asyncio.CancelledError is a BaseException, so
a disconnect cancelled mid-report returned the cancellation as a value and
the caller dropped it, which suppresses the cancellation of whatever task
owns the disconnect. It now catches Exception, and names the adapter's own
api_key in the ElevenLabs fallback warning rather than a variable the adapter
never reads.

* fix(tests): give the realtime span test its own api key

connect() now refuses to dial with no credential at all, so a test that
inherited an empty OPENAI_API_KEY from the runner started failing in CI while
passing on any machine that exports one. The key is stated in the test.

Also folds in three review points: one import style for scenario.voice.broker
in the mint tests, and explicit pytest types on both new conftest hooks.

* fix(voice): repair two voice e2e wrappers that could never pass

Both predate this branch and both fail the on-demand voice job for reasons
that have nothing to do with what a demo does.

test_demo_openai_realtime_user_e2e_success imports a demo that guards itself
with a module-level sys.exit(0) while cross-adapter audio bridging is
unimplemented. The import raised SystemExit and pytest reported a hard
failure, so a demo that says 'skipped' in its own message reads as broken.
The wrapper now skips on that signal, which is the case TESTING.md already
names as a legitimate skip: code that has not shipped.

test_demo_recording_playback_wav_written imported OUT_DIR from a demo that
never defined it, so the test raised ImportError before it ran. Recordings
move through save_demo_recording, which writes segments/, full.wav and
manifest.json under the demo's own directory. That path is now a public
demo_recording_dir the writer and the test share, rather than a second copy
of the layout in the test that had already drifted from a file name the
writer stopped using.

Also uses one import style for the broker in the mint tests, reading the
patched function off the adapter module so the wrapped object is exactly what
the adapter calls.

* fix(voice): state the zeros when closing an unused realtime session

A mint that succeeded followed by a socket that never opened was closed with
an empty usage object, and the gateway refuses that with HTTP 400. Its parser
reads a usage report by looking for input_tokens or output_tokens and rejects
a body carrying neither, so the report never landed, the failure went into a
debug log, and the session stayed open holding one of the key's slots until
its grace expired. Measured against the live gateway: the mint returned
req_3f9b8c6a8ce63ac29307f4e64fff49 and the closing report came back 400.

The counts are now stated as zero, which parses and closes the record at the
number that is true for a credential that opened no socket. One
close_unused_realtime_session in the broker owns that shape, so the adapter
and the routing check cannot drift apart on it.

The TypeScript adapter posts the same empty object from _closeUnusedSession
and has the same defect. That is on the other side of the split and is left
to the JavaScript branch.

* fix(tests): close a minted session even when an assertion fails

Three review points. The realtime-user wrapper now re-raises a nonzero
SystemExit, because the same demo also exits with a message when its
environment is incomplete, and missing infrastructure is a failure rather than
a skip. The routing check moves its response assertions into a try and closes
the session in a finally, so a failing assertion no longer leaves a booked
record holding one of the key's slots; the close result is asserted after the
finally so a cleanup error cannot hide the assertion that got there. The mint
test helpers carry explicit types.

* fix(voice): sum realtime usage across responses, not just the last one

OpenAI reports usage per response. Measured against the live API on
2026-08-21: two turns on one socket reported output_tokens 4 and 4, and
input_tokens 120 and 135, rather than a running total. The adapter kept only
the last response.done, so a multi-turn session closed its spend record with
its last turn's numbers and every earlier turn billed as nothing.

accumulate_realtime_usage sums every numeric leaf and recurses into the
detail objects, so the audio, text and cached breakdowns a gateway prices
separately add up alongside the totals. No key list, so a count the vendor
adds later accumulates rather than being dropped.

The TypeScript adapter keeps the last response.done and its comment states
the opposite of what the vendor does, so it has the same defect. That file is
on the other side of the split and is left to the JavaScript branch.

* fix(voice): close a brokered session that never produced a response

* fix(ci): a shared budget outage stops blocking unrelated pull requests (#892)

The examples suite makes real model calls on one gateway virtual key with a
daily spend cap. When the cap is hit the gateway answers 402 budget_exceeded
and every test in the suite fails at once. That suite feeds a required check,
so a pull request whose own 1088 JavaScript and 1219 Python tests all passed
was blocked from merging by a shared resource it never touched.

The suite now runs behind scripts/ci/examples-suite-gate.sh, which separates
"the suite could not run" from "the suite ran and disagreed".

What it deliberately does NOT do is turn the suite green and walk away. This
repository has already been bitten by a suite that cannot fail: #893 records
fork pull requests reaching a green required check with nothing having read the
changed file. So a budget outage is reported as a warning and in the run
summary, both saying the suite did not run rather than that it passed, and it
is tolerated only where tolerating it costs no coverage.

That last part is the rule that keeps it honest. A budget outage lasts until
the daily window resets, so a pull request that CHANGES the examples stays red
through one: nothing verified the change, and a green check would say
otherwise. Only pull requests that touch nothing the suite covers are let
through, because for them the suite was never evidence in the first place.

Telling those apart needed a new `examples` filter, and wiring it surfaced a
trap the composite action documents and nothing enforced: a filter key consumed
without being declared in the action's outputs lands as the empty string, which
is worse than either true or false because it looks wired and answers nothing.
scripts/validate-examples-gate.sh now turns that comment into a check for every
filter in every workflow, not just this one.

Eight mutations, each caught. The gate's own harness is asserted on the number
of checks it ran, because the first version returned a path on stdout, which
$(...) swallowed along with every PASS line: six cases reported nothing while
the summary still said all checks passed.

Closes #892

* fix(ci): a manual usage refresh names the pull request's own commit

Two defects found in review of this change.

A manual refresh passes a pull request number and nothing else. The workflow
fell back to `github.sha` for the commit line, which on a dispatch is the
branch the refresh ran from, not the pull request. Every manually refreshed
comment would therefore end "Updated for <default branch sha>", naming a
commit that has nothing to do with the work it reports. The same gap defeated
the fork guard: `github.event.pull_request` is absent on a dispatch, so the
job-level condition let every dispatched number through, fork or not.

The pull request answers both questions, so the script now asks it. The
workflow passes the head sha only when the event carries one, and an empty
value sends the script to the API for the head sha and the head repository.
A head branch in another repository, or a head repository that is gone with
a deleted fork, is refused.

Second, the comment search stopped after ten pages. A pull request with more
than a thousand comments would hide the marker past the cap, the search would
report "no existing comment", and the upsert would POST a second report
rather than update the first. GitHub's `Link` header is the listing's own
end signal, so the walk follows rel="next" and stops when there is no next.

fix(#922): always report a scenario run as finished, and make event delivery retry (#928)

* test(#922): add event delivery reliability spec

* fix(#922): always report a scenario run as finished, and retry event delivery

A run that failed on a script assertion could end without a
SCENARIO_RUN_FINISHED event when the finished-emit path itself raised, so
the run stayed open in the UI forever. Event delivery also had no working
retry: the reporter swallowed every transport failure, so the bus retry
ladder never saw an error and a lost event was lost silently.

- Report the run as finished exactly once on every exit path of run(),
  through a guard set as soon as the event reaches the stream. The catch
  now takes BaseException, so a cancelled or interrupted run still
  reports, and the original error always propagates.
- Build error results defensively: if assembling the result raises, fall
  back to a minimal result so the event still goes out.
- The reporter raises on transport failures and non-2xx responses so the
  bus can retry. An unconfigured endpoint or api_key still skips silently.
- The reporter accepts a shared httpx.AsyncClient. The bus worker thread
  now owns one event loop and one client for its lifetime instead of a
  new loop and client per event.
- The retry ladder logs a warning instead of printing, stops early on a
  permanent 4xx (408 and 429 still retry), and drops the event after the
  last attempt so delivery can never fail the run.
- The worker sweeps the queue before exiting, and drain() revives a dead
  worker while the queue is not empty, so the exit race cannot deadlock
  drain(). drain() also resets the bus so it can be reused.

* fix(#922): mirror the finished-event and delivery fixes in the JS SDK

Same defects as the Python SDK: a failed run could end without a
RUN_FINISHED event, one failed event terminated the whole event stream,
and a dropped RUN_FINISHED left drain() waiting on its 300 second
timeout before run() could return.

- Report the run as finished exactly once, through a guard set as soon as
  the event reaches the stream, and build error results defensively.
- postEvent throws on network failures and on a non-2xx response, with
  the HTTP status attached, so the bus can retry. A reporter that is not
  configured still returns {}.
- Retry and error handling moved inside the concatMap, per event: retry
  with backoff, skip retries for a permanent 4xx (408 and 429 still
  retry), then drop the event. One failed event no longer takes the
  stream and every event behind it down.
- drain() resolves on stream completion as well as on RUN_FINISHED, and
  removes the bus from the static registry.

* fix(#922): address review on the event delivery reliability fixes

Keep the worker's HTTP client private to the worker that owns it, and
pass it to each post instead of writing it onto the shared reporter. A
2xx answer whose body is not JSON now counts as delivered in both SDKs,
so an accepted event is never posted twice. The JavaScript failure log
redacts inline base64 audio the way the Python one already did. The
drain waits for an ending worker before it starts a replacement and
bounds its queue wait, so a lost worker cannot hang a run. The minimal
error result reads its fields through defaults, so a failure in the
run-started emit still produces a terminal event.

* fix(#922): report a finished run when the setup before the run fails

Voice connect and modality resolution ran before the guarded scope, so
a failure in either one left the run with no terminal event. Both now
run inside it. Each worker owns the shutdown event it watches, so a
worker that is still ending cannot be un-signalled by the event that
drain installs for the next one, and the outgoing thread reference is
kept until it actually ends. Reporter subclasses take the http_client
argument of the base signature.

* fix(#922): set the finished guard before the event reaches the stream

on_next delivers to each subscriber in turn, so a subscriber that
raised after the bus already took the event left the guard unset and
the outer error path published a second finished event. A regression
test raises from the emit path after delivery and asserts one event.

* fix(#922): complete the stream and close the trace when publication raises

A finished event whose publication raised skipped the stream completion
and the trace close, so a subscriber kept waiting and the trace was
never exported. Both now run from a finally, each guarded, and the
trace is read through a default for the path where reset has not run.

* test(#922): annotate the run-finished test helpers

The adapter role attributes and the reporter patch helper carried no
explicit types.

* fix(#922): import Subject from rx.subject.subject

rx pins its public surface such that 'from rx.subject import Subject'
fails at import time on 3.12 CI, while 'from rx.subject.subject import
Subject' is the path the executor itself uses.

* fix: pin zod to 3.25.74 for @openai/agents-core compatibility

zod 3.25.76 broke the @openai/agents-core@0.16.0 import used by the
realtime example, failing every CI run with 'Cannot read properties of
undefined' at @openai/agents-core/src/types/protocol.ts:802. This failure
is inherited from main and not introduced by this PR, but it blocks CI.
The pin follows the same pattern as the existing security/version pins in
the pnpm overrides block.

* Python SDK: the event worker delivers the queue left behind when drain stops waiting

drain() releases the caller after its deadline, but the shutdown signal it
then sends made the worker exit as soon as its in-flight request ended,
leaving every event still queued with no worker to take it. A run started
event that spends its retry ladder on a transient failure could therefore
orphan the run finished event queued behind it, even after delivery
recovered. The worker now sweeps the remaining queue before exiting on
shutdown, so the caller's wait stays bounded while delivery continues on
the non-daemon worker thread.
